intro: Thailand is a year-round destination, but timing changes the experience a lot — rain, heat, hotel prices and crowds. This guide covers the seasons, month-by-month weather, and how the two coasts differ.

blocks.html: Short answer: The best window for most of Thailand is November to February — cool, dry and comfortable for both cities and beaches, but it is high season with crowds and higher prices. March to May is very hot, while June to October is the rainy season (showers come in bursts, not all-day rain) with lower prices and fewer people.

blocks.text: Gulf vs Andaman — different rainy timing

blocks.html: A detail many miss: Thailand’s two coasts do not get rain at the same time. The Andaman side (Phuket, Krabi, Phi Phi) is wettest around May to October, while the Gulf side (Samui, Phangan, Tao) gets its heaviest rain late in the year, around October to December. So if one coast is in its rainy season, the other may have better weather.

blocks.title: Songkran: fun but books out
blocks.html: Mid-April is Songkran, the nationwide water-fight new year. It is great fun, but accommodation and transport book out fast and prices rise — if you come then, book well ahead.

faq.q: What is the best month to visit Thailand?
faq.a: November to February is best overall — cool, dry and comfortable for cities and beaches — but it is high season with crowds and higher prices. To avoid crowds and save money, try the early rainy season like June.

faq.q: Is Thailand worth visiting in the rainy season?
faq.a: Yes. Rain usually comes in short bursts, not all day; the landscape is lush, prices are low and crowds thin. Just avoid sea activities on rough days and allow extra travel time.

faq.q: Which coast should I pick for the beach?
faq.a: From May to October the Gulf coast (Samui, Phangan, Tao) often has better weather than the Andaman; from November to April the Andaman (Phuket, Krabi) is at its clear-water best.
